alignments.note: Vocative construct noun; the ASV writes no O or ye, so the noun takes only its own word (rule 36).
Nomen rectum with the relational of, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
Interrogative מַה has its own English word, so the copula is not fronted to it (rule 17's last limit).
Finite הָיָה rendered by the present copula is; the marginal Or, was does not change the alignment.
Construct rendered attributively as the vine tree, so no of is written (rule 28); the construct noun keeps tree.
The one written the stands at the left edge of the phrase and is taken by the present article morpheme (rules 29, 47).

Comparative מִן rendered by the two-word more than, one rendering of which no other morpheme owns a part (rule 30). Headed on than as the word carrying the preposition's own lexeme (rule 24); heading on more is the competing reading, since more is what marks the comparison.
Rectum rendered attributively with no of written (rule 28).

One substantive rendered by the two-word vine branch; by rule 31's subtraction the specifier vine is the ASV's addition to a word that already names the thing, so the head is branch, as תַּנִּין → sea monsters heads on monsters.
Finite הָיָה rendered by the copula of the relative clause.
The ASV renders the rectum arthrously and writes a the before each word, so nothing is fronted: the construct takes a supplied the (rule 29).
The article takes the the standing before its own word (rule 29).
Rectum with the relational of, discontinuous around the article's the (rules 19, 25).

review_notes: Two construct chains are handled differently because the ASV renders them differently: עֵץ־הַגֶּפֶן attributively (rule 28) and עֲצֵי הַיָּעַר with of and two the's (rule 29's arthrous clause).
The comparative מִן takes both more and than as one rendering; the note records the competing head.
